newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Nov 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY - Some 20 tonnes of garbage shipped from the United States were dumped secretly in a Hong Kong landfill without going through Customs or approval from the Environmental Department.
-- SING TAO DAILY - China Vice-Premier Qian Qichen will be in Hong Kong on December 11 to host the selection of Hong Kong's first post-handover leader.
-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO - China is pushing its space development projects to strengthen its competitiveness in international space technology in the next century.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - The residential property resale market was active in October. Trade experts expect both new and second-hand property markets to be active in November.
-- Recent research showed 90 percent of the business community was confident about Hong Kong's present economy and 70 percent was confident about it after the mid-1997 handover.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Two contracts in the controversial Western Corridor Railway project has been awarded to a consultancy linked to a pro-Beijing former civil servant and vocal critic of the project.
-- A leading industrialist said that one in 10 textile companies inspected by joint US-Hong Kong customs teams had been "blacklisted" because of alleged transshipment violations.
-- Chinese companies have received approval to issue 25 billion yuan worth of corporate bonds this year, almost double last year's amount.

-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD - The Law Reform Commission said banks and creditors would be held at bay under proposals to give troubled companies a breather when facing disgruntled creditors.
